messages.content:
Risk: Accountability
Description: Assigning responsibility for an action taken by an agentic AI system is difficult due to the complexity of agents and the number of external resources, tools or agents they interact with.
Concern: 'Without properly documenting decisions and assigning responsibility, determining liability for unexpected behavior or misuse might not be possible.'
Policy: Medical Professional Impersonation

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000005: Act — A Process in which at least one Agent plays a causative role.
  Siblings: Change, planned process, history
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/PartiesAndSituations/Agent: agent — something autonomous that can adapt to and interact with its environment
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HarmfulHowTo: Harmful How-To — Step-by-step instructions for activities that cause property destruction, physical harm, or enable illegal intrusion when executed by unauthorized individuals.
  Siblings: CBRN Information, Drug Synthesis, Dual-Use Research Concern
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0000520: emotional liability AE — a sensory capability AE that has an outcome of emotional liability
  Siblings: hyperesthesia AE, sensory loss AE, sensation of blood flow AE
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/ResponsibleParty: responsible party — legal person acting in a role that has some formal responsibility
  Siblings: legally delegated authority, auditor

axes.rationale: The 'Act' class represents processes involving agents, which is central to understanding accountability in AI systems as it involves assigning responsibility for actions taken by these agents.
The 'responsible party' class directly relates to the concept of accountability by defining roles with formal responsibility, which is crucial for assigning liability in AI actions.
